extracted.intended_audience: appellate counsel handling appeals from PTAB to the Federal Circuit (practitioners preparing joint appendices)
extracted.subtask_short: preparing joint appendix for PTAB appeal
extracted.subtask_description: Practical best-practice steps for coordinating, compiling, paginating, and submitting a master and final joint appendix in appeals from PTAB proceedings to the Federal Circuit, consistent with Federal Circuit Rule of Practice 30 and the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for initial designation (45 days before appellant's principal brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should attempt to agree on the initial designation of appendix materials at least forty-five days before the appellant’s principal brief is due. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(1)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first step; early agreement helps avoid conflict and streamline preparation. Draft letters coordinating this timeline are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant fallback designation and statement of issues (30 days rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parties cannot agree on the initial designation, the appellant must serve its designation on the appellee with a statement of issues no later than thirty days before the appellant’s principal brief is due. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(1)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve the appellant's designation plus statement of issues to preserve the schedule when agreement cannot be reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellee counter-designation window (14 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellee has the opportunity to counter-designate record materials for the appendix within fourteen days after service of appellant’s designation. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(1)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appellant designates the entire record, this step is often obviated, saving effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate the entire PTAB record
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the record in PTAB proceedings is limited, the parties should designate the PTAB record in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating the entire record simplifies the process, reduces risk of omitting valuable material, and generally obviates the need for counter-designations even if it produces a larger master appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all exhibits, including demonstratives
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant should take care to designate all exhibits, including demonstrative exhibits, from the PTAB proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to designate demonstratives or other exhibits may omit important record material; include them to ensure completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include ministerial filings (do not omit entries of appearance etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although it may be tempting to omit ministerial filings, such as entries of appearance, the simplicity of designating the entire record and the risk of inadvertently omitting valuable record material outweighs the benefit of a slightly smaller master appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate seemingly 'ministerial' documents to avoid accidentally excluding materials that become important on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix materials must be ordered chronologically (satisfy FRAP 30(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix materials should be ordered chronologically to satisfy Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 30(d). See Fed. Cir. R. 30(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chronological ordering both complies with the rules and aids navigation; numbering should match that ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare appendix pagination and summary table after designations
rubrics_metrics.description: After designations are complete, the appellant should prepare appendix pagination and a summary table containing those numbers. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(2)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree to extend the deadline for this task; preparing a summary table helps parties and the court locate cited materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties may agree to extend Rule deadlines (without leave) so long as briefs' filing times aren't affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are permitted to agree to extend the Rule deadlines without leave of the court so long as it does not affect the time for filing a brief. See Fed. Circ. R. 30(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide recommends extending the pagination/summarization deadline to the deadline for the appellant's opening brief to streamline exchanges; this is commonly done in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve a master appendix with the appellant's opening brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant should serve a master appendix when it files its opening brief; this master appendix should include all of the designated materials (i.e., all materials from the PTAB proceeding). See Fed. Cir. R. 30(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a comprehensive master appendix at opening brief filing lets the appellee cite consistent page numbers in its responsive brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master appendix numbering and stamping conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The master appendix should be stamped with appendix numbers centered in the bottom margin, begin with 'Appx', and the designated material must be numbered by the automated Bates numbering feature of the software used to convert the document into a PDF. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(c)(2) and Quick Reference: Formal Brief Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated Bates numbering to ensure sequential, machine-readable numbering. Put the 'Appx' prefix and center the numbers in the bottom margin per the cited guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required initial contents/order of master appendix (judgment/order, patents, certified list first)
rubrics_metrics.description: The master appendix should begin with the judgment or order being appealed from, the patent(s) being challenged, and the certified list, in that order. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(a)(1)(A)–(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After those items, remaining materials should follow chronologically per FRAP 30(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for adding inadvertently omitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: If either party identifies additional material from the record inadvertently not captured in the original designations, the parties should agree to add such materials to the end of the appendix at the time of the parties' briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreeing prospectively to append omitted material at filing time avoids disputes and preserves a single master appendix numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final joint appendix submission deadline (7 days after reply brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must submit to the court a final joint appendix seven days after filing its reply brief. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan to prepare and finalize the joint appendix within this tight post-reply timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final joint appendix should be pared to only materials actually cited in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare the final submission, the parties should each separately identify the appendix materials actually cited in each brief; after resolving discrepancies, the appellant should pare the master appendix down to only these cited materials and submit that as the joint appendix. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party should proactively list cited materials to speed agreement; the joint appendix is intended to contain only cited materials for the court's convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant bears ultimate responsibility for preparing the joint appendix and should seek early agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing the joint appendix is ultimately the appellant’s responsibility. See Fed. Cir. R. 30(b)(5). The appellant should seek to forge agreement with other parties early in the appeal briefing, ideally before or when the appellant initially designates appeal material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should lead coordination efforts (e.g., use a draft coordination letter). Early leadership reduces disputes and deadline pressure.
